items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Anita Brown, who was a very beautiful girl, and she was very popular... Well, these women were all entertainers that could sing and dance

ctx.x: Would you call these ladies jazz singers?

Well, I guess you would call them that. No, they weren't just jazz singers. Some of them were -- at that time it was a thing where they used to go to the tables, you know. They used to have -- the clubs were all, naturally, intimate spots, and they would go around to the various tables. Now, they'd work with a piano player and they'd go around to the tables and sing intimate songs. So I don't think this would be so much called jazz, for all of these people that I've talked about. But this is what people wanted,…

Some of them -- another singer that comes to mind was Betty Treadwell. I think I mentioned Betty. She was one of the singers from the Breakfast Club, over the Club Alabam. And these singers worked, they did pop and some of them did a little dancing. Anita Brown, who was a very beautiful girl, and she was very popular, and another girl was Billie Brown, and another one was Bonnie Bryant. Well, these women were all entertainers that could sing and dance, you know, and every little spot, as I say, featured…
